text:
ravi_kumar: Quick help please - relocating to Tokyo next week. Embassy requires vaccine + TB proof for my visa appointment in 4 days. I paid for an occupational TB test and booster at a local clinic (receipt in JPY). Also added my spouse in January but no ID card arrived. Can we get: 1) an embassy-acceptable coverage/vax confirmation, 2) retro electronic dependent ID, and 3) how to submit the JPY claim?

maria_peopleops: Congrats on the move! :tada: We can issue an expedited Coverage & Vaccination Confirmation PDF. When did you add your spouse? That affects physical card issuance.

ravi_kumar: Added Jan 15 during OE. Embassy appointment is Fri.

sasha_benefits: For the claim: upload the original receipt, a short English translation, and proof of payment (bank/cc statement) to the Benefits portal under "Out-of-country medical claims" and check the foreign currency box. We'll convert rates.

ben_hr_ops: Because spouse was added during open enrollment we can generate a retro electronic ID (PDF) now. Send full name + DOB and I'll email it.

ravi_kumar: Spouse: Asha Kumar, DOB 1992-04-03. Please send PDF to ravi.k@redwood.com.

claims_bot: Note: International/occupational claims require complete docs. Standard processing 10-15 business days; expedited triage ~2-3 days after upload.

sasha_benefits: For embassy acceptance: our cover PDF is usually fine if they only need confirmation of coverage and vaccination dates. If the consulate asks for lab values (e.g., Quantiferon) you must get the clinic's signed report. If clinic can add a one-line English note "Occupational TB screen: negative; vaccine given" that's sufficient.

maria_peopleops: Ben will send the e-ID PDF. Ravi, once you upload claim docs tag @sasha_benefits in the portal and we'll mark it expedited for the embassy timeline.

ravi_kumar: Uploaded receipt_jp.pdf, tb_stamp_jp.jpg, payment_stmt.png. Tagged Sasha. Thanks all!

claims_bot: Claim OC-2026-521 created and flagged for expedited triage. Expect triage within 48-72 hours.
